title: Black queer men in Westminster | BLKOUT in Westminster
metaDescription: For Black queer men in and around Westminster — Soho, Pimlico, Marylebone, Victoria: what's here, what's beside us, what's worth the journey, and a community-owned door into BLKOUT.

landmark.alt: Pencil sketch of the Elizabeth Tower with the BLKOUT roundel set into its clock face

hero.kicker: One community. Many doors. This one is Westminster's.
hero.heading: BLKOUT in Westminster
hero.standfirst: BLKOUT is a community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — and Westminster is a borough we've stood in ourselves. On 15 February 2019 we presented the inaugural Berto Pasuka Lecture at the National Portrait Gallery — a sold-out night honouring Britain's first Black-led dance company, given by David McAlmont. A year earlier, Let's Talk: Black Boy Joy ran at Ku Bar in Soho in association with BLKOUT and 56 Dean Street, with Marc Thompson among the speakers. Around 16,500 Black residents live in the borough. This door is for the Black queer men among them.

quiz.heading: Know your Westminster?
quiz.sub: Three questions. No prizes except the stories.

questions.q: In February 2019, BLKOUT presented the inaugural Berto Pasuka Lecture at which Westminster institution?
questions.reveal: The National Portrait Gallery — a sold-out night, 'Portrait of a Black Queer Briton', given by David McAlmont in honour of Berto Pasuka, the Jamaican-born dancer who co-founded Les Ballets Nègres, Britain's first Black-led dance company.

questions.q: In April 2018, 'Let's Talk: Black Boy Joy' ran in association with BLKOUT at which Soho venue?
questions.reveal: Ku Bar, Leicester Square — an open-mic night by and for queer people of colour, run with 56 Dean Street, with Marc Thompson among the speakers. Genuinely our own history in this borough.

questions.q: Black-owned queer venue COVEN has just moved into Soho — which borough did it start in?
questions.reveal: Hackney Wick — COVEN opened its Soho headquarters on 30 Old Compton Street, the former G-A-Y Bar site, on 19 June 2026. Proof a night can start anywhere and still end up centring its people in the heart of London.

scores.three: Westminster knows its own Soho. Now help us keep it current.
scores.two: Close. There's more here than the tourist map shows.
scores.low: All the more reason to walk through the door below — the history is the easy part to catch up on.

worthTheJourney.heading: Worth the journey
worthTheJourney.intro: Black queer men have never let a borough boundary decide where community happens. Where you're centred, not just welcome:

entries.name: Black Beetle Health
entries.note: The UK's only public health charity focused specifically on health inequalities for LGBTQ+ Black people and people of colour — resources, research and signposting, reachable from anywhere.

services.heading: Look after yourself
services.intro: Free, confidential, no GP needed, no judgement — and your business stays yours.

entries.name: Sexual Health London (SHL)
entries.note: Free, discreet home test kits and PrEP by post anywhere in London — order online, nothing to explain to anyone.

entries.name: 56 Dean Street
entries.note: Soho's LGBTQ+ specialist sexual health and HIV service — Europe's largest, seeing around 11,000 visitors a month, most of them gay and bisexual men. Right here in the borough.

entries.name: Naz Project London
entries.note: Sexual health, HIV support and wellbeing for Black, Global Majority and LGBTQ+ communities, working across Westminster, Kensington & Chelsea and Hammersmith & Fulham.

entries.name: Find your nearest NHS clinic
entries.note: Every NHS sexual health service near you — testing, treatment, PrEP — searchable by postcode.

numbers.heading: The numbers nobody counts
numbers.body: The 2021 Census recorded 8.1% of Westminster's population — around 16,500 people — as Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African, up from 7.5% in 2011. Westminster doesn't rank among London's ten largest Black populations, so we don't have a dossier figure for it — but applying the same estimate we use elsewhere, that's roughly 350 to 550 Black queer men living in the borough right now. Small as a share of one of London's most international boroughs. Still thousands of us.
numbers.history:
Westminster's Black queer history includes one of our own proudest nights — and a much longer fight over who gets to be seen at Pride.

Pride in London's parade runs through Westminster every year, past Trafalgar Square and Whitehall. Black queer organising has been inside that history for two decades: in 2005, 'Proud to B ME' brought Black and minority ethnic Pride communities together, with an after-party at the Pitcher and Piano on William IV Street, by Trafalgar Square. By 2008, the Black Gay Men's Advisory Group (BGMAG) — chaired by our founder Rob Berkeley — was negotiating directly with Pride London over funding for Black and BME floats and a dedicated BME stage.

On 15 February 2019, BLKOUT presented the inaugural Berto Pasuka Lecture at the National Portrait Gallery — sold out, part of LGBT History Month. Berto Pasuka, born Wilbert Passerley in Jamaica in 1911, moved to London and co-founded Les Ballets Nègres in 1946 with Richie Riley — Britain's first Black-led dance company. David McAlmont gave the lecture, 'Portrait of a Black Queer Briton', in five acts set to two centuries of music by Black composers. It was built as the first in a series, and it remains a genuine high point of our own record in this borough.

A year earlier, in April 2018, Let's Talk: Black Boy Joy ran downstairs at Ku Bar, Leicester Square, in association with BLKOUT and 56 Dean Street — an open-mic night by and for queer people of colour, with Marc Thompson among the speakers. Black queer London has moved through Soho in other ways too: our own archive carries a 2018 profile of Jay Jay Revlon, the ballroom scene builder behind English Breakfast and the House of Revlon, and a mention of a 2016 vogue battle held as a vigil in Soho Square. In 2025 the council's own archive started platforming Black queer artists through events like Black, Queer & Young.

Most recently: a Black-owned queer venue called COVEN, which started in Hackney Wick, opened its Soho headquarters — bar, café, community hub and five-floor club — at 30 Old Compton Street on 19 June 2026, on the former G-A-Y Bar site. Full details are in the directory below. If you were at the Gallery in 2019, in that room at Ku Bar in 2018, on a BME float, or you know a chapter we've missed, the panel further down is where you tell us.

archive.intro: Westminster runs through our own writing and our own nights out — Let's Talk: Black Boy Joy at Ku Bar in 2018, and a ballroom-scene profile carrying a Soho vigil. Those pieces are in the story archive and being brought back online; when they are, they'll be listed here.

faq.q: Where can I meet other Black queer men in Westminster?
faq.a: Start with the door on this page — you'll hear about everything as it happens. COVEN's new Soho headquarters is in the directory below, and BLKOUT's national community is open to you today. If a few Westminster men want a table in the borough, we'll help hold it.

faq.q: Where can I get an STI test or PrEP in Westminster?
faq.a: Sexual Health London posts free test kits and PrEP to any London address, no GP and no conversation required. 56 Dean Street is right here in Soho, and Naz Project London covers the borough for wider sexual health and wellbeing support.

BLKOUT is one community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — with a door in every borough. We're registered in Croydon and we belong wherever our men are. We were part of a night in Soho back in 2018, before this page existed.

faq.q: I'm not out. Can I still come?
faq.a: Yes. Come as you are — nobody at this door asks you to be anything first, and your business stays yours.

faq.q: Is the history on this page accurate?
faq.a: It's checked against the public record and dated so you can see when we last looked. If we've got something wrong — or missed a chapter you were part of — the panel at the bottom is where you tell us, and the page changes.

door.heading: Be met
door.tender: Come as you are. We answer.
door.intro: Leave your name and we'll keep you posted about Westminster — what's on, what's starting, and how to be part of it. This goes to BLKOUT, a co-operative owned by its members. No engagement machinery, nothing sold onward — just a community that answers.

truer.heading: Make it truer
truer.intro: We've found one night that was genuinely ours — and the people here know the rest of this borough's story best. If a group has folded, a night has moved, or we've missed a chapter you were part of — tell us. Corrections get credited, if you want the credit.
